observation.description: Running the versioned-seed reset (the fix for the A2-f7 raw-reset wedge) against a sessions-mode app took three undocumented discoveries: (1) an adminToken-only client cannot offer the auth-client protocol ('authClientProtocol v1 requires browser, agent, or explicit external-bearer custody'), so the admin client must ALSO carry a session bearer via createExternalSessionClient(url, { bearerToken, adminToken }); (2) previewVersionedSeed/resetInstallVersionedSeed default requestedMode to dev, so a sessions app refuses with SNAPBACK_SEED_CROSS_MODE_UNSUPPORTED until requestedMode:'sessions' is passed explicitly on every call; (3) the active expectedDataVersionStream is discovered from preview.current.dataVersionStream, which no guide page shows. Once known, the loop is excellent: reset-install restored the literal seed with a receipt (operation, outcome, resetDeletedRows, dataVersionStream) and the next snapback dev start accepted the database — no SNAPBACK_SEED_NONEMPTY_UNTRACKED wedge.

competitorOutcome.description: Not competitor-comparable — the versioned-seed lifecycle is a Snapback differentiator once reachable; frozen arms hand-rolled cleanup scripts.

mustNotRegress: The reset-install receipt and the predecessor-stream gate (exact {state:'present',value} matching).
smallestCoherentFix: A sessions-mode versioned-reset snippet in the acceptance or versioned-seeds guide page: external-bearer+admin client construction, requestedMode:'sessions', preview-discovered stream; ideally default requestedMode from the active app mode instead of dev.
acceptanceWitness: A cold agent reading the versioned-seeds page resets a sessions-mode app to its literal seed on the first try, and the next dev start accepts the database.
